executive_summary: Grants for Dutch technology startups validating entry into a new foreign business market with a qualified local partner. Technical, commercial, economic or legal barriers can be addressed for a mature self-developed technology, with prototype testing allowed but product development, general market research and sales promotion excluded. The regulation caps support at EUR 25,000 and 50% of eligible costs, with at least EUR 50,000 in eligible project costs. Applications run from 2 March to 31 December 2026 while budget remains, after a mandatory RVO quick scan; projects last at most one year. RVO plans support for 40 validations in 2026, split equally between developing countries and other countries.
status_rationale: The RVO Marktvalidaties page (Wat is een marktvalidatie?) and Staatscourant 2026-7891 sections 4.4(d) and 7(4) support foreign-market validation of mature startup technologies with a qualified local partner. Inspection and grid-equipment applications could benefit Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) and the procurement needs of the 2GW Program, an interpretation of the broad technology scope rather than an energy-specific objective. Sections 3 and 4.2 define the enabling local partner as non-Dutch and require Dutch funded consortium participants to export or invest in support of the SME, so the call establishes no suitable domestic end-user or test-site route for TenneT Netherlands. Type 3 category C3.2 reflects possible benefits through suppliers’ products.
